paragraphs: Weak supervision provides clues about the right prediction without necessarily supplying a complete label for every example. Those clues can take different forms, making it difficult to build methods that work across settings. This paper introduces GLWS, a framework that handles partial labels, aggregate statistics, pairwise observations, and unlabeled data within a common learning formulation.

Its central tool is Expectation-Maximization, which organizes learning around information that is observed and information that remains uncertain. The computational contribution combines a nondeterministic finite automaton with a forward-backward algorithm. Weak supervision is represented through the automaton, turning the design of a learning procedure into a problem of modeling the available constraints.

The authors report that this construction reduces computational demands from quadratic or factorial complexity found in existing solutions to linear complexity. Across 11 weak supervision scenarios, GLWS also demonstrates strong performance and versatility. The contribution therefore joins two practical aims: accommodating different kinds of incomplete supervision and making the associated computations easier to scale.
icml-2024-a-general-framework-for-learni.tldr: GLWS represents varied forms of weak supervision with automata to simplify learning and reduce computational complexity.

paragraphs: Federated learning must contend with both information leakage and participants that deliberately submit harmful updates. Combining encrypted computation with robust aggregation can address these concerns together, but the paper identifies shortcomings in existing systems: expensive computation, exposure of the final model to the server, and dependence on a single aggregation rule.

AegisFL builds its design around operations shared by advanced robust aggregation algorithms: vector inner products, lengths measured with the L2 norm, and averages. It packs the relevant values into ciphertexts in a way tailored to RLWE-based fully homomorphic encryption. Under this packing scheme, constructing the required aggregation computation needs only one ciphertext multiplication.

The system also permits changing the robust aggregation rule, addressing the rigidity that can leave a fixed rule vulnerable to attacks designed specifically for it. The global model remains available only to honest clients. Experiments across datasets and adversary settings support the system’s effectiveness and efficiency, connecting its encryption design to practical federated learning behavior.
icml-2024-aegisfl-efficient-and-flexible.tldr: AegisFL makes encrypted, robust federated learning more efficient while supporting changes to the aggregation rule and protecting the final model from the server.

paragraphs: Choosing a Linux kernel configuration is a difficult optimization problem because the kernel exposes more than 15,000 options. Evaluating configurations is costly, and a poor choice can prevent the operating system from starting. AutoOS uses large language models to automate this customization for different Artificial Intelligence of Things application scenarios.

The framework treats configuration as optimization over a dynamic tree, drawing on the directory structure of the kernel configuration process. A state machine guides traversal through a repeated sequence of observation, pruning, proposal, action, and correction. This gives the language model a structured process for narrowing the search space and correcting configuration choices while supporting successful boot-up.

The experiments show automatic customization and optimization without human effort, with performance improvements reaching up to 25% over vendor-provided configurations. That figure describes the reported upper improvement, rather than a uniform gain across scenarios. The central contribution is the combination of language-model assistance with a structured search and correction procedure for an unusually large configuration space.
icml-2024-autoos-make-your-os-more-power.tldr: AutoOS combines language models with structured configuration search to automatically optimize Linux kernels, reporting gains of up to 25% over vendor configurations.

paragraphs: Understanding sequential data can require recovering hidden processes whose effects unfold over time. Existing approaches often assume that observations preserve enough information to reverse the mapping from hidden variables to measurements. This assumption is restrictive when observation loses information, as when a three-dimensional scene becomes a two-dimensional image or current perception incorporates earlier inputs.

The paper develops an identifiability theory for recovering independent hidden components from nonlinear, non-invertible mixtures. CaRiNG turns that theory into a learning method by using temporal context to recover information missing from individual observations. Its training procedure incorporates the theory’s conditions, so the recovery guarantees remain tied to those conditions rather than applying to every information-losing process.

Synthetic experiments show that CaRiNG can reliably identify the causal process even when the observation-generating mapping is non-invertible. The authors also report improvements in temporal understanding and reasoning in practical applications. The key implication is that information lost in a single observation need not preclude recovery when useful information remains available across time.
icml-2024-caring-learning-temporal-causa.tldr: CaRiNG uses temporal context to recover hidden causal components under theoretical conditions that allow information-losing observation processes.

paragraphs: Imitation learning trains a policy from expert demonstrations without requiring reward signals. Behavioral cloning predicts an action given a state, which is simple but can generalize poorly. Modeling states and actions together can improve generalization, yet the paper identifies slow inference and manifold overfitting as difficulties with relying on that joint distribution.

Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning combines the two views of expert behavior. A diffusion model learns the expert distribution, while the policy is trained with both the usual behavioral cloning loss and a diffusion-based loss representing the joint distribution. The policy therefore receives guidance about the demonstrated action at a state and about how state-action combinations fit expert behavior overall.

Experiments report better performance than baselines across continuous control tasks involving navigation, robot arms, dexterous manipulation, and locomotion. Additional experiments examine the limitations of conditional-only and joint-only modeling and compare generative models. Ablations support the proposed design choices, providing evidence that combining the two training signals is useful across the evaluated control settings.
icml-2024-diffusion-model-augmented-beha.tldr: DBC combines behavioral cloning with a diffusion-based training signal to improve imitation learning across several continuous control domains.

paragraphs: Linear attention offers a route to reducing Transformer computation, but changing the attention mechanism can require extensive retraining. That cost is especially consequential for large pretrained language models. DiJiang addresses the conversion problem: adapting an existing standard Transformer into a model with linear complexity while keeping the required training cost low.

The method uses frequency-domain kernelization to approximate the attention computation. Its weighted Quasi-Monte Carlo sampling method comes with a theoretical claim of improved approximation efficiency. Discrete Cosine Transform operations provide the basis for the kernelization, further reducing the computational burden of training. These components connect the quality of the approximation with the cost of obtaining it.

Experiments report performance comparable to the original Transformer alongside substantially lower training costs and faster inference. In particular, DiJiang-7B achieves comparable results to LLaMA2-7B across various benchmarks at about one-fiftieth of the training cost. The reported result supports converting pretrained models efficiently while retaining benchmark performance, rather than requiring the attention redesign to begin with extensive training.
icml-2024-dijiang-efficient-large-langua.tldr: DiJiang converts pretrained Transformers to linear-complexity models using frequency-domain kernelization, with comparable reported performance and much lower training costs.

paragraphs: Early exiting accelerates a language model by allowing predictions before computation passes through every layer. Making that idea useful at large scale requires training and inference procedures that fit distributed execution. EE-LLM addresses this systems challenge with a framework built on Megatron-LM that supports early-exit models using large-scale three-dimensional parallelism.

Its training innovations include a lightweight way to backpropagate the early-exit objective through a pipeline-parallel system. It also uses resources that would otherwise be idle in the pipeline schedule to perform computations associated with early-exit layers. For inference, the framework supplies two early-exit approaches compatible with the key-value caching used during autoregressive generation.

The analytical and empirical evaluation reports negligible additional computation during training compared with standard language-model training. It also reports substantial inference acceleration without reduced output quality in the evaluated settings. The contribution is thus a practical route for scaling early exiting: the auxiliary training work, distributed scheduling, and generation-time caching are handled together within one framework.
icml-2024-ee-llm-large-scale-training-an.tldr: EE-LLM scales early-exit language models through distributed training and cache-compatible inference, reporting minimal training overhead and faster generation.

paragraphs: Learning several tasks together requires choosing how to balance their objectives. A Pareto front describes trade-offs where improving one objective comes at a cost to another. Instead of producing only a few separate solutions, recent methods approximate a continuous range of trade-offs by combining base networks. The paper addresses the difficulty of scaling that strategy to many tasks.

The proposed architecture combines a main network with several low-rank matrices. This reduces the number of parameters needed to represent the Pareto manifold and helps extract features shared across tasks. The authors also introduce orthogonal regularization as an additional component intended to improve performance. Together, these choices provide a more compact way to learn a family of task balances.

Extensive experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, especially on datasets containing many tasks. This pattern directly supports the method’s scaling motivation: a compact representation of task variation becomes particularly useful as the number of objectives grows. The contribution concerns both parameter efficiency and the quality of the learned trade-off solutions.
icml-2024-efficient-pareto-manifold-lear.tldr: A shared network with low-rank matrices learns task trade-offs more compactly and improves reported performance, especially when many tasks are involved.

paragraphs: Molecular models must respect how physical quantities behave when coordinates are rotated or translated. Invariant features remain unchanged, while equivariant features transform consistently with the coordinate change. GeoMFormer provides a common architecture for learning both kinds of representation, addressing the authors’ concern that existing approaches often depend on specialized, costly modules.

The model uses standard Transformer components arranged into two streams, one for invariant representations and one for equivariant representations. Carefully designed cross-attention passes information between them. This lets the streams enrich each other while maintaining their different geometric roles, bringing both types of information into the same molecular modeling framework.

The authors show that many earlier architectures can be understood as particular instances of GeoMFormer, supporting its claim to generality. Experiments report strong results on invariant and equivariant tasks across different types and scales. These findings support the usefulness of a flexible shared design for molecular learning, rather than requiring an unrelated architecture for each kind of geometric prediction.
icml-2024-geomformer-a-general-architect.tldr: GeoMFormer links invariant and equivariant Transformer streams to learn molecular representations that respect geometric constraints.

paragraphs: GRATH aims to improve the truthfulness of an existing language model through repeated self-supervised refinement. The motivation is that even capable models can produce false content and achieve only modest results on truthfulness benchmarks. The method creates a training process centered on distinguishing correct answers from incorrect answers to the same question.

It starts with question prompts from outside the target domain and generates paired truthfulness data. Each pair contains a question together with a correct and an incorrect answer. Direct preference optimization then trains the model using the difference between those answers. GRATH repeats the process, refining the truthfulness data and updating the model across iterations.

Experiments with different seven-billion-parameter models report improved truthfulness without compromising other core capabilities. On TruthfulQA, the reported MC1 and MC2 accuracies are 54.71% and 69.10%, respectively, exceeding the compared 70-billion-parameter models. These results show that the proposed refinement process can substantially improve measured truthfulness without relying on an increase in model size.
icml-2024-grath-gradual-self-truthifying.tldr: GRATH repeatedly generates contrasting answer pairs and applies preference optimization to improve language-model truthfulness.

paragraphs: This paper examines kernel ridge regression when the input distribution changes between training and evaluation, a setting called covariate shift. Its focus is importance reweighting: adjusting how much influence training examples receive. The authors study this in high dimensions, where understanding the resulting prediction error requires examining the structure of the kernel itself.

They derive asymptotic expansions for kernels under covariate shift and separate error into bias and variance. The analysis shows that reweighting allows variance to decrease. Its effect on bias is more sensitive: different choices of regularization scale can produce substantially different behavior. Thus, a variance benefit does not by itself describe the entire prediction error.

Both components can be characterized through the spectral decay of a data-dependent regularized kernel that combines the original kernel matrix with a reweighting matrix. This supplies an interpretation of importance weighting as a form of data-dependent regularization. The paper also develops expansions for kernel functions and vectors, providing analytical tools for studying this shifted-distribution setting.
icml-2024-high-dimensional-kernel-method.tldr: The paper interprets importance reweighting as data-dependent regularization and analyzes its distinct effects on bias and variance under covariate shift.

paragraphs: Click logs reflect both relevance and the way users examine ranked results. Unbiased learning to rank tries to disentangle these influences by modeling click generation. This paper shows that fitting clicks does not always recover the underlying relevance, despite earlier empirical successes, and that the failure can substantially harm ranking performance.

The authors define identifiability as recovering true relevance up to a scaling transformation, which is sufficient for the pairwise ranking objective. Within their analysis, they establish an exact criterion: relevance is recoverable if and only if an identifiability graph derived from the dataset is connected. A disconnected graph can leave the model unable to recover the relevant relationships.

Two proposed remedies, node intervention and node merging, modify the dataset to restore graph connectivity. Experiments on simulated data and two real-world ranking benchmarks support both the theoretical characterization and the effectiveness of these interventions. The practical message is that the structure of the available click data matters, alongside how well a model fits those clicks.
icml-2024-identifiability-matters-reveal.tldr: The paper characterizes relevance recovery through graph connectivity and proposes dataset interventions for otherwise unidentifiable ranking problems.

paragraphs: Estimating an average privately becomes harder when communication must also be compressed. Existing approaches often start from a different geometric setting and adapt to L2 geometry, which can worsen the leading constants in mean squared error. Methods with favorable communication-privacy trade-offs can also be difficult to use in streaming privacy systems.

The paper introduces privacy accounting for a sparsified Gaussian mechanism that incorporates randomness from sparsification into the privacy noise calculation. It works directly in L2 geometry, with errors that rapidly approach those of the uncompressed Gaussian mechanism. This ties the privacy analysis to the compression procedure rather than treating compression randomness as irrelevant to privacy.

The authors extend the scheme to matrix-factorization methods for streaming differential privacy and provide an accountant for DP-FTRL optimizers. Empirically, they report at least a hundredfold improvement in compression for DP-SGD across several federated learning tasks. The work therefore addresses both estimation accuracy under communication constraints and compatibility with privacy mechanisms that accumulate information over time.
icml-2024-improved-communication-privacy.tldr: A new privacy accountant incorporates sparsification randomness to improve compressed private mean estimation and support streaming privacy optimizers.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization involves two linked optimization problems, and decentralized versions distribute the work across participants. Existing algorithms can require nested rounds of communication to coordinate their computations. The paper identifies this intensive information exchange as a major obstacle to providing rigorous differential privacy when the underlying data are sensitive.

The proposed stochastic algorithm avoids nested loops of information exchange. The authors establish both differential privacy and accurate convergence, presenting this combination as a first for decentralized bilevel optimization. Their motivation is especially notable because existing privacy methods for even single-level decentralized learning can require sacrificing convergence accuracy.

The theoretical analysis covers nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex settings and characterizes convergence rates in each. It also quantifies how privacy affects the rate, separating the ability to converge accurately from the speed of doing so. Experiments on machine learning models support the algorithm’s effectiveness. The central contribution is a communication design that makes privacy compatible with accurate convergence while explicitly accounting for its cost in convergence rate.
icml-2024-locally-differentially-private.tldr: A decentralized bilevel algorithm avoids nested communication loops and provides privacy with accurate convergence while quantifying the effect on convergence speed.

paragraphs: Interactions among several language-model agents can improve reasoning, but generating multiple rounds of responses is expensive. MAGDi aims to transfer the benefits of those interactions into a smaller model that can be used efficiently on its own. It treats the relationships among agents’ reasoning steps as useful training information.

The method represents multi-agent interactions as graphs and augments the student model with a graph encoder. Training combines next-token prediction, a contrastive objective distinguishing correct from incorrect reasoning, and a graph-based objective capturing interaction structure. This gives the student supervision about both reasoning content and how the different contributions relate to one another.

Across seven commonsense and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, MAGDi outperforms several distillation methods using one or multiple teachers. It also reports an order-of-magnitude efficiency advantage over its teachers. Further analyses find better generalization to tasks outside the training domain, positive scaling with student size and strength, and larger gains when using self-consistency. These results support preserving interaction structure as part of the knowledge transferred to smaller models.
icml-2024-magdi-structured-distillation-.tldr: MAGDi distills graphs of multi-agent reasoning into smaller models, improving reasoning performance while reducing inference cost.

paragraphs: A transition model describes how an environment changes, making it important for sequential decision-making from previously collected data. Standard forward models tend to favor smooth relationships. That preference can be a poor match for environments whose transitions have abrupt discontinuities or regions where their behavior changes sharply.

The paper proposes Energy-based Transition Models, which represent transition probabilities implicitly through a scalar energy function. This provides a flexible way to describe the distribution of possible transitions and capture complex dynamics. The reported modeling results show accurate fits to discontinuous transition functions and improved generalization to transition data outside the training distribution.

The authors then test whether these modeling improvements help downstream decisions. Their models improve off-policy evaluation accuracy and significantly outperform other evaluated methods on the DOPE benchmark. They also improve offline reinforcement learning, outperforming prior algorithms on D4RL Gym-Mujoco tasks. Together, these findings connect a more flexible transition representation with benefits in both assessing policies and learning policies from offline data.
icml-2024-offline-transition-modeling-vi.tldr: Energy-based transition models capture complex dynamics and improve reported offline policy evaluation and reinforcement learning results.

paragraphs: In performative prediction, deploying a model changes the data distribution it will encounter. Optimizing such a model therefore requires accounting for its influence on the environment. This paper addresses settings where the objective need not be convex in model parameters, the model’s effect on the distribution is unknown, and gradient information is unavailable.

The proposed framework rewrites the objective in terms of parameters describing the induced data distribution. A two-level procedure then operates without gradients. One level optimizes over distribution parameters; the other learns a model that induces the target distribution selected at that iteration. This separates choosing a desirable distribution from finding a model that produces it.

Under the paper’s stated mild conditions, this reparameterization turns the nonconvex objective into a convex one and enables provable regret guarantees. The regret bound is sublinear in the number of performative samples and polynomial in the dimension of the model parameters. The result establishes a conditional route to learning with limited feedback while avoiding several assumptions commonly used in earlier analyses.
icml-2024-performative-prediction-with-b.tldr: Optimizing over induced data distributions enables conditional regret guarantees for performative prediction without known distribution responses or gradients.

paragraphs: Federated learning exchanges model updates, but those updates can reveal information about clients’ training data. Gradient inversion attacks attempt to reconstruct that data, and recovering sample labels can help the reconstruction. This paper introduces RLU, a label recovery method designed to work beyond the restrictive assumptions used by earlier approaches.

RLU analyzes the relationship between labels used during a training round and the resulting changes to the model’s output layer. It turns that relationship into a least-squares problem for estimating labels. The reported performance extends to settings with multiple local training epochs, heterogeneous client data, different optimizers, and different training objectives.

The method achieves near-perfect label recovery for untrained models, which the authors identify as the most vulnerable case. Across datasets, architectures, and data heterogeneity scenarios, it consistently outperforms existing baselines. It also improves reconstructed images according to PSNR and LPIPS. These findings show that label leakage remains consequential under the more realistic local training conditions examined in the paper.
icml-2024-recovering-labels-from-local-u.tldr: RLU recovers training labels from federated model updates across varied local training settings and improves subsequent data reconstruction.

paragraphs: Transformers can make accurate predictions while remaining overconfident about them. Gaussian processes offer a way to represent uncertainty, but applying them to attention introduces a structural issue: attention kernels are asymmetric, whereas earlier approaches use symmetric kernels. Computing the resulting posterior distributions can also be expensive at large scale.

KEP-SVGP addresses both issues through a kernel singular value decomposition. The decomposition produces two sets of singular vectors, which induce a pair of sparse variational Gaussian processes that characterize the attention kernel’s asymmetry. Using a small set of associated eigenfunctions allows posterior computation to rely on inverting a diagonal matrix of singular values, reducing its time complexity.

The authors derive an evidence lower bound that jointly trains the variational parameters and network weights. Experiments report strong performance and efficiency on benchmarks covering ordinary evaluation, distribution shift, and out-of-distribution inputs. The contribution is an uncertainty-aware attention formulation whose mathematical structure accommodates asymmetry while simplifying an otherwise costly part of Gaussian-process inference.
icml-2024-self-attention-through-kernel-.tldr: KEP-SVGP models uncertainty in self-attention while accounting for asymmetric kernels and reducing posterior computation costs.

paragraphs: SelfIE addresses the challenge of understanding what a language model represents internally while producing an answer. It enables a model to describe its own hidden embeddings in natural language, drawing on its existing ability to answer questions about a passage. The goal is to make internal representations accessible through explanations expressed as text.

The framework interprets open-world concepts rather than restricting interpretation to a fixed inventory of predefined categories. The paper presents cases involving ethical decisions, the internalization of prompt injection, and the recall of harmful knowledge. These descriptions provide a basis for examining internal reasoning and for designing interventions that target the represented concepts.

The authors introduce two control methods built on this approach. Supervised Control edits open-ended concepts while requiring gradient computation for only an individual layer. Reinforcement Control extends reinforcement learning from human feedback to hidden embeddings and is presented as erasing harmful knowledge without supervision targets. The paper thus connects natural-language interpretation of embeddings with methods for changing the model’s internal behavior.
icml-2024-selfie-self-interpretation-of-.tldr: SelfIE turns hidden language-model embeddings into natural-language interpretations and uses them to support interventions on internal concepts.

paragraphs: Learning to control multiple entities in a three-dimensional environment becomes difficult as the joint state space grows exponentially with the number of entities. This paper explores reducing that complexity through local views that remove redundant geometric information. Its proposed architecture is the Subequivariant Hierarchical Neural Network, or SHNN.

SHNN first uses task assignment to dynamically divide the global environment into local graphs at the entity level. It then applies subequivariant message passing to construct local reference frames. These representations compress redundancy associated with geometry, particularly in environments affected by gravity. The architecture therefore combines a decision about which entities belong together with a structured representation of their local physical relationships.

The authors also introduce MEBEN, a benchmark suite designed to capture varied multi-entity reinforcement learning problems and their geometric structure. SHNN substantially improves over existing methods on these proposed benchmarks. Ablation studies support the importance of both task assignment and subequivariance, connecting the reported gains to the architecture’s two central mechanisms.
icml-2024-subequivariant-reinforcement-l.tldr: SHNN combines task-based local graphs with geometric structure to improve multi-entity reinforcement learning on the proposed MEBEN benchmarks.

paragraphs: Partial differential equations describe evolving systems across science and engineering. Neural networks offer a way to represent their solutions, but achieving high accuracy remains difficult, particularly when solving an initial value problem forward in time. TENG is a method designed to improve the accuracy of this neural-network-based time evolution.

The framework combines ideas from time-dependent variational principles and optimization-based time integration through natural gradient optimization. The authors develop TENG-Euler and higher-order variants such as TENG-Heun, giving the framework multiple time-integration algorithms aimed at precision and efficiency. The emphasis is on accurately performing the optimization associated with successive stages of the evolving solution.

Evaluations include the heat equation, Allen-Cahn equation, and Burgers’ equation. The paper reports performance exceeding current leading methods and machine precision in the step-by-step optimizations. That precision claim specifically concerns those optimization steps; it should not be read as a claim that every complete PDE solution has machine-precision error. The findings support natural gradient optimization as a useful component of highly accurate neural PDE solvers.
icml-2024-teng-time-evolving-natural-gra.tldr: TENG uses natural gradient optimization for neural PDE time integration, achieving machine precision in reported step-by-step optimizations.

paragraphs: A time series can contain only a few short regions that determine its class. Standard supervised classification does not fully account for this sparsity and locality, even when using powerful neural networks. TimeMIL reframes multivariate time series classification as a weakly supervised problem, aiming to locate the relevant patterns while preserving their temporal relationships.

The method uses multiple-instance learning, connecting a sequence-level classification problem with patterns within the sequence. Its time-aware pooling explicitly models temporal correlations and ordering. A tokenized Transformer and a specialized learnable wavelet positional token supply the mechanism for incorporating that temporal information, so the model can account for when patterns occur as well as their content.

The authors report that TimeMIL surpasses 26 recent state-of-the-art classification methods. This supports the usefulness of the weakly supervised formulation for the evaluated tasks. The contribution brings together two needs that can otherwise pull apart: identifying localized evidence and understanding how that evidence fits into the ordered structure of an entire time series.
icml-2024-timemil-advancing-multivariate.tldr: TimeMIL uses time-aware multiple-instance learning to classify multivariate sequences from sparse local patterns and their temporal relationships.

paragraphs: Step-by-step language-model reasoning often follows a forward-only structure, making earlier mistakes difficult to revisit. Thought Rollback introduces a framework in which the model can adapt its reasoning structure as it works. The aim is to keep problem-solving effective when intermediate responses contain errors or hallucinations.

The central mechanism analyzes thoughts for errors and allows a return to a previously mistaken thought for revision. The resulting trial-and-error history is included in the prompt to guide subsequent reasoning. Starting from a simple prompt without human annotations, the model progressively explores and revises its path toward a solution instead of committing permanently to each earlier step.

Experiments on mathematical problems and multi-task reasoning report state-of-the-art results for solving rate and interaction cost. On MATH, GPT-4 with Thought Rollback exceeds the reported best solving rate by 9%. These results provide empirical support for revisiting earlier reasoning decisions and using the revision history to guide further work, without establishing that rollback guarantees a correct answer on every problem.
icml-2024-toward-adaptive-reasoning-in-l.tldr: Thought Rollback lets language models revisit mistaken reasoning steps and use their revision history to improve problem-solving.

paragraphs: Meta-tuning adds an optimization stage to a foundation model to improve its ability to adapt to new tasks. In vision, earlier versions have shown limited success and can perform poorly on tasks outside the training distribution. Sparse MetA-Tuning, or SMAT, addresses this weakness by learning which pretrained parameters to use for each task.

Inspired by sparse mixtures of experts, SMAT automatically isolates task-specific subsets of parameters during meta-tuning. This makes the sparsity pattern part of what is learned. The paper analyzes why learned patterns outperform hand-designed ones and shows that the amount of sparsity plays a central role in balancing generalization within and outside the training distribution.

The method establishes reported state-of-the-art results on Meta-Dataset combined with additional out-of-distribution tasks, both without task-specific gradient adaptation and with gradient-based adaptation. These findings support the claim that sparse meta-tuning can improve vision foundation models beyond parameter-efficient fine-tuning in the evaluated settings. The central insight is that choosing parameter subsets adaptively can strengthen transfer across tasks.
icml-2024-unleashing-the-power-of-meta-t.tldr: SMAT learns sparse task-specific parameter subsets to improve vision-model transfer, including performance on out-of-distribution tasks.
